MLS® uses Dewdney Deroche as a sub-area name, but the Fraser Valley Regional District has no published boundary for it. Dewdney and Deroche both lie within the Fraser Valley Regional District rather than the City of Mission.

The FVRD’s Electoral Area G page says Area G includes the communities of Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island and Nicomen Island east of Mission, with a 2021 Census population of 2,090 and a size of 119 km².
DFO’s directions place Dewdney approximately 10 kilometres east of Mission along Lougheed Highway (Highway 7).

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Fraser Valley Regional District and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).
General information only.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Dewdney Deroche

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The FVRD’s Electoral Area G page says Area G includes the communities of Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island and Nicomen Island east of Mission, with a 2021 Census population of 2,090 and a size of 119 km².

The FVRD has an Official Community Plan for Electoral Area G (Bylaw No. 0866, 2009, adopted April 28, 2009). It covers Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island and Nicomen Island, so check it and the FVRD zoning bylaw for any lot you are looking at.

The FVRD’s Hatzic Valley Official Community Plan (Area F, Bylaw No. 0999, 2010) covers the area north of Hatzic Lake, including Hatzic Prairie, Durieu and McConnell Creek. It does not cover Dewdney or Deroche.
The Dewdney Area Improvement District has managed water levels for flood protection since 1948, and the lake and slough drain through flood gates and a pump station.

A 1982 Environment Canada flood-control analysis describes the Dewdney Area Improvement District, on the north bank of the Fraser River, as protecting 1,760 hectares of rural, residential and agricultural land.
The Province’s dike inventory includes dike drawings and reports for the Dewdney / Norrish area east of Mission.
The Hatzic Lake plan says Hatzic Island lies within the Fraser River floodplain and is susceptible to localized flooding.
Mission has route numbers 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39 on BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley route list, but not one of them names Dewdney or Deroche.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Dewdney Deroche

parts.t: Check who sets the zoning.

Dewdney Deroche falls under the Fraser Valley Regional District and not the City of Mission. To learn what the zone and plan designation permit at a specific address, speak to the FVRD planning department.
Check the ALR status.
Look up the exact address on the Agricultural Land Commission map before you plan anything on farmland.
Check the flood and hazard rules.
Ask the FVRD how the mapping for floodplains, creeks and slopes applies to the address, and whether a development permit is required.
Check the water and septic.
Ask for well and septic records and the last inspection.
Check the road and services.
Ask who maintains the road, what fire protection covers the address, and what is a long drive away.
Confirm the school catchment.
Ask School District 75 for the exact address.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.
Where are Dewdney and Deroche?
Dewdney Deroche is an MLS® sub-area name. The Fraser Valley Regional District doesn’t publish a boundary for it.

The FVRD’s Electoral Area G page says Area G includes the communities of Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island and Nicomen Island east of Mission, with a 2021 Census population of 2,090 and a size of 119 km².
DFO’s directions place Dewdney approximately 10 kilometres east of Mission along Lougheed Highway (Highway 7).
How do I get around from Dewdney or Deroche?
None of the routes on the Central Fraser Valley list from BC Transit names Dewdney or Deroche. The Mission routes it shows are 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, plus 39.
The nearest West Coast Express station is Mission City Station, at 33200 North Railway Avenue in Mission.
Which schools are near Dewdney and Deroche?
Dewdney Elementary is at 37151 Hawkins-Pickle Rd and Deroche Elementary is at 10340 N Deroche Rd, both Kindergarten to 6.
SD75’s catchment policy puts both in the Hatzic Middle School catchment.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
Mission Public Schools (School District 75)
, which publishes a catchment map.
What is there to do outside?
Dewdney Regional Park is at 7840 River Road South, Deroche, and Inch Creek Hatchery is at 38620 Bell Rd, Dewdney.
The Mission Library, at 33247 Second Avenue, is the Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Mission.
What plan covers Dewdney and Deroche?

Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island and Nicomen Island fall under the FVRD’s Electoral Area G Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 0866, 2009). The FVRD’s Hatzic Lake Management Plan, a separate plan for the lake, also touches Hatzic Island.
